brief: How to protect 4 hours of deep work in a calendar full of meetings.

slots.headline: How to Protect Four Hours of Deep Work Inside a Packed Calendar

slots.title: Block the Hours
slots.body: Treat your deep-work window like an immovable client meeting. Put it on the calendar first, before anyone else can claim that slot. Consistency trains colleagues to respect your focus time.

slots.title: Say No Politely
slots.body: Not every meeting deserves your presence. Decline invites that lack an agenda or a clear decision. Offer asynchronous updates instead to protect your cognitive bandwidth.

slots.title: Set Expectations Early
slots.body: Share your focus hours with your team at the start of each week. Add a calendar note explaining you are unavailable for quick chats. Visibility prevents frustration.

slots.title: Close the Inbox
slots.body: Notifications fragment attention and extend shallow work. Silence email and chat during your deep block. A single distraction can cost twenty minutes of recovery time.

slots.title: Batch Meetings Together
slots.body: Cluster calls into one or two afternoons rather than scattering them. This creates uninterrupted mornings for demanding projects. Batching also reduces context-switching fatigue.

slots.title: Audit Your Calendar
slots.body: Review your week every Friday to see where time leaked. Remove recurring meetings that no longer serve a goal. Small adjustments compound into hours saved.

slots.headline: Take Back Your Focus Hours
slots.body: Small calendar changes create space for meaningful work. Guard four hours and watch output multiply.
